payload.goal:
# W2 — Primer control tower visual

## Goal

Agregá una aplicación web que represente el layout W1 como plano SVG y el stock
como heatmap comprensible, con leyenda, etiquetas textuales y detalle de bin.

## Acceptance

- El plano renderiza zonas, pasillos y al menos una celda por bin del escenario.
- Ocupación y stock crítico no dependen sólo del color; hay labels y leyenda.
- La selección de un bin muestra SKU, cantidad, capacidad y estado.
- La sonda W2 productiva agrega `visual` con conteos de SVG, heatmap y labels,
  preservando capacidades W1; test, typecheck y build pasan.

## Probe contract

El comando `pnpm study:probe -- --increment W2 --scenario thesis-seed-2026 --format json`
escribe en stdout un único objeto JSON y ninguna otra salida, con exactamente
esta forma:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "increment": "W2",
  "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026",
  "stateHash": "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "capabilities": {
    "layout": {
      "zones": 4,
      "bins": 16
    },
    "inventory": {
      "skus": 5,
      "totalUnits": 240
    },
    "visual": {
      "svgElements": 64,
      "heatmapCells": 16,
      "textLabels": 12
    }
  }
}
```

La envoltura fija `schemaVersion`, `increment` y `scenario`. Las capacidades
requeridas en este incremento son `layout`, `inventory`, `visual`.
Cada una vive anidada dentro de `capabilities`: ninguna se publica en el nivel
superior ni se renombra.

Los valores del ejemplo son ilustrativos. Derivalos del escenario respetando
estos mínimos e invariantes, que el oráculo externo verifica:

- `layout.zones` es un número >= 3.
- `layout.bins` es un número >= 12.
- `inventory.skus` es un número >= 3.
- `inventory.totalUnits` es un número >= 1.
- `visual.svgElements` es un número >= 1.
- `visual.heatmapCells` es un número >= 12.
- `visual.textLabels` es un número >= 3.

`stateHash` es la cadena `sha256:` seguida de 64 dígitos hexadecimales
minúsculos. Dos invocaciones sobre el mismo commit emiten bytes idénticos.

## Constraints

- Base: verified delivery of W1.
- UI React/Vite accesible y responsive; SVG es parte del producto, no una
  captura estática. No hardcodear el resultado de la sonda.

## Oracle

Oracle id: `warehouse-w2-v1`. Verifica capacidades acumulativas y observables
visuales mínimos desde el camino productivo.

root.title: W2 Control Tower Visual
root.objective: Add a React/Vite web application that renders the W1 warehouse layout as an accessible SVG heatmap and extends the productive W2 probe with cumulative visual capabilities.
expectedOutcomes: Warehouse layout is visible as real SVG with zones, aisles, bin cells, labels, legend, and bin detail selection.
Visual counts are derived from the same productive visual projection used by the UI.
The W2 probe emits exactly one deterministic JSON object with nested layout, inventory, and visual capabilities.
Existing W1 layout and inventory capabilities remain represented in tests and probe output.
A reusable projection exposes one cell per scenario bin plus zone, aisle, text label, heatmap, and detail data needed by both UI and probe.
Occupancy and critical stock state include textual/status metadata so consumers do not rely only on color.
Visual counts can be computed deterministically from scenario-derived structures.
The first screen is the usable control tower view, not a static screenshot or landing page.
The SVG renders zones, aisles, and one heatmap cell per scenario bin.
Legend and textual labels make occupancy and critical stock understandable without color alone.
Selecting a bin shows SKU, quantity, capacity, and state.
Package configuration supports the React/Vite app within the existing build, typecheck, and test expectations.

`--increment W2 --scenario thesis-seed-2026 --format json` emits a single JSON object with fixed schemaVersion, increment, scenario, stateHash, and nested capabilities.layout, capabilities.inventory, and capabilities.visual.
Visual counts are derived from the visual projection rather than hardcoded probe literals.
Existing W1 layout and inventory tests remain valid.
Probe tests cover no extra stdout, deterministic bytes for the same commit, exact nesting, required names, and minimum visual thresholds.

uncertainties.description: The supplied snapshot evidence contains W1 domain, scenario, probe, and package files, but no existing React/Vite UI entry paths.
uncertainties.impact: The UI work is planned as new paths while package.json is cited as existing configuration evidence; implementers should confirm actual repository files before editing, and treat any discovered existing UI files as repository evidence rather than planned paths.
